// diagnostic L2401

Jet.PositionalBoolParameter

Public function `{fn_name}` has a positional `Bool` parameter `{param}`.

What

Public function `{fn_name}` has a positional `Bool` parameter `{param}`.

Why

Positional booleans are easy to transpose: `connect(host, true, false)` is a guessing game. Argument labels make the intent clear at the call site.

Fix

Callers can use `{param}: true` to document intent; or give the parameter a default value so it can be omitted. No action required — this is advisory.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.PositionalBoolParameter: Tests/UILint/inferred_never_return.warn.

Warning: Jet.InferredNeverReturn: Public function `fail` always diverges but does not declare `Never`
  --> Tests/UILint/inferred_never_return.jet:4:1
    |
  4 | fail: fn(message: String) { panic(message) }
    | ^^^^
 Why: Inferred divergence is useful to callers but is not part of the written API contract
 Fix: Write `-> Never` as the return type, for example `fail: fn() -> Never`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.InferredNeverReturn
